name: Webwinder Path
summary: Webwinder Path winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, linking Malaka'jin with Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods.

sections.title: A Treacherous Thoroughfare
sections.body: Webwinder Path runs from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake through the lower Stonetalon Mountains. Thick webs hang among the trees and along the jagged cliffs. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Travelers must watch their step along the winding route.

faq.answer: Webwinder Path runs north from Malaka'jin, the Darkspear troll outpost, toward Mirkfallon Lake.

faq.q: Why is it called Webwinder Path?
faq.answer: Webwinder Path takes its name from the many arachnids in the region. Spiders spin webs high in the trees and along rocky ledges beside the road.
Venomous spiders weave webs above the road, while thunder lizards, highland rams, and other mountain creatures roam nearby.

faq.q: Is Webwinder Path safe to travel?
faq.answer: Webwinder Path is dangerous, with fierce, territorial predators along the way. It also passes Malaka'jin, a Horde camp, putting Alliance travelers coming from the Barrens at risk.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can use this overland route beside Malaka'jin to reach the deeper valleys of Stonetalon.
As a hunter, you can scout the path for thunder lizards, mountain rams, and venomous spiders to tame.
